summary: The Aceman is Mini's five-seat electric crossover, slotted between the Cooper hatch and the Countryman, and Australian reviewers broadly agree it delivers the brand's go-kart handling in a shape that finally has usable back seats — Chasing Cars scored the SE 8.0 and made it its 2025 Premium Small Car of the Year. The recurring objection is price against size: $60,990 before on-roads buys a 4.08-metre car when a larger Volvo EX30 opens at $49,990, and Mini cleared the cheaper Aceman E from the local range in 2025 at $51,990 drive-away, leaving the SE and JCW E as the only two grades. Opinion splits on the ride, which is firm on the standard 19-inch wheels, and on whether the JCW E's extra 30kW justifies $5,000 and a 51km range penalty.
pros: Sharply tuned front-drive chassis that reviewers rate as genuinely fun — Chasing Cars called the SE a 'tenacious corner carver' and scored it 8.0/10, well clear of a BYD Atto 2 or Zeekr X on driver appeal
Far more usable than the Mini Cooper Electric it shares a platform with: five seats and a 300-litre boot expanding to 1005 litres, against the Cooper's four seats and 210 litres
406km WLTP from the SE's 49.2kWh usable pack is competitive for a 4.08-metre car, and Chasing Cars still recorded 351km in real-world Australian testing
Both grades sit under the $75,000 FBT exemption cap that applies from April 2027 — even the $65,990 JCW E has just over $9,000 of headroom, so a novated lease keeps the full exemption

8-year high-voltage battery warranty on top of the 5-year unlimited-kilometre vehicle warranty (CHOICE and CarExpert's launch review give 160,000km; CarExpert and CarsGuide spec tables list 100,000km)
cons: Expensive for the metal: $60,990 for the SE against $49,990 for a longer-range Volvo EX30 and $46,080 for a Zeekr X, both roomier cars
95kW peak DC charging is modest — CarsGuide measured 31 minutes for 10-80 per cent and called it disappointingly slow next to the EX30's 153kW
Firm damping on the standard 19-inch wheels is the most consistent criticism in Australian reviews; CarExpert flagged a busy, jittery ride at speed and Chasing Cars found it fatiguing around town
Rear-seat space and outward vision are compromised for a five-seater — CarsGuide notes tight rear legroom and a large B-pillar blind spot, and tyre noise is 'far from best in class'
Resale risk is real: Mini sold off the entry Aceman E at $51,990 drive-away and deleted it within months of launch, and Mini's EV volume in Australia is small
